tested:
Wave 21 U2 (NPX-819). netplex ships an Alpine qcow2 as well as the Docker image, and
the two are DIFFERENT runtimes with different hardware: /netplex/images/qemu/linux/
alpine-base-3-19-1/virtioa.qcow2 is a real KVM guest. Before this key existed, the
name matcher found the Docker "alpine" profile just below, image-manager threw it
away as a runtime mismatch (a QEMU upload cannot use "emulator": "docker") and the
image fell back to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE - so a device netplex actually ships had no
curated hardware at all. Same shape and same reason as "vyos-qemu" sitting beside
the Docker "vyos" entry; the longer key wins the longest-match rule, so the Docker
entry is untouched for real Docker nodes.
Live boot 2026-09-05 (probe: -machine pc -cpu host -m 512 -smp 1, virtio disk, NO
NICs at all, system QEMU 10.2.1) - reached, verbatim:
Welcome to Alpine Linux 3.19
Kernel 6.6.16-0-virt on an x86_64 (/dev/ttyS0)
localhost login: root
localhost:~#
So: text console on the first serial port, root with no password, and it boots with
zero network interfaces (nothing in the guest waits on a NIC). Wave 21 classes it C
(shell) - its config channel is the generic shell dialect, marker-only fidelity,
exactly like the other Linux images netplex ships.
